Hello, this is Diane from the counselling office. Every year I record this for our international students, because every year somebody arrives in my office in week six thinking something is wrong with them. Nothing is wrong with you. Around week five or six the novelty stops and the tiredness starts, and everything that felt charming in September feels annoying in October. That is culture shock, and it has a shape: excitement, then irritation, then normal life. If I could give you one piece of advice, it would be this: do not make big decisions in week six. Do not decide that you hate the food, or the school, or the country. Wait two weeks and decide then. Almost nobody decides the same thing.

Hey, it's Nico. So, you asked me what I would change if I did this year again. Honestly, two things. First, I would speak more in the first month. I was so worried about sounding stupid that I said almost nothing until November, and by then people had already decided I was the quiet one. If I started again, I would be the annoying one who talks too much, one hundred percent. Second, I would say yes to more things. Somebody invites you to a hockey game on a Tuesday and it is cold and you have homework, and you say no. Say yes. That is where everything happens. Everything else, the food, the weather, the school, you get used to in three weeks anyway.

In the first weeks everything feels new and exciting, and Lais says yes to everything. Around week five the tiredness arrives and small things start to feel annoying. She talks to another exchange student on a bench outside the cafeteria. He tells her what he would do differently if he started the year again. Two weeks later the same things feel normal and she stops thinking about them.
